question.knowledge_point: Solving a Trigonometric Equation Involving Cosine with Non-Special Angles
question.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions of the equation $\operatorname{cos}⁡x=-\frac{7}{9}$ for $0\le x<2\pi ,$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$ to the nearest integer?
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{7}{9}) & =2.461\,918…≈2.461\,9\end{aligned}
$$

Since $2.461\,9$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=2.461\,9.$

Our first solution lies in the second quadrant and has a reference angle of 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{R}=\pi -2.461\,9 & ≈0.679\,7.\end{aligned}
$$

 Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=0.679\,7.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14061537/assets/eafc9be7094c9c0ccdf167cc737d494efec40014a89ad793f7ed34ea5eed94ae.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +0.679\,7 \\  & ≈3.821\,3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=2.461\,9\cdot 3.821\,3≈9
$$

to the nearest integer.
